model.label: Terrain horizon · Sun upper limb · Earth centre
model.definition: Sun visible = the upper limb of the solar disc is above the local terrain horizon. Earth visible = the centre of the Earth is more than 0° above the terrain horizon (direct-to-Earth line of sight). The observer is a 2 m mast above the surface. Sun and Earth positions come from spice ephemerides in the MOON_ME frame; the horizon comes from the pgda terrain model (bruteforce method); the Moon is airless (no refraction).
limits: Samples every 1 h: each rise or set time is accurate to +-1 h, and an event shorter than one step can be missed.
The terrain horizon comes from a digital elevation model of finite resolution and radius; rocks and relief smaller than its pixels are not modelled.
Visibility is geometric only: no power-system, thermal, antenna pattern or radio link-budget model, and no relay satellites.
Not a landing-safety assessment: slopes, hazards and surface conditions are not evaluated.

conventions.time: UTC ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ; ranges are [start, end) with exclusive end; sample t represents [t, t + step)
conventions.azimuth: deg clockwise from local north, [0, 360) (N = 0, E = 90)
conventions.elevation: deg above the local horizontal plane (airless, body centre)
conventions.distance: km (no distance field in this response; GET /series has sun_dist_km / earth_dist_km)
conventions.height: surface_height_m: m above the 1737.4 km reference sphere; observer_height_m: m above the surface
